title: Close the tenant functional-completeness gaps found by the 2026-10-27 tenant review
goal: The 2026-10-27 read-only tenant review (docs/reviews/TENANT_FUNCTIONAL_COMPLETENESS_REVIEW_2026-10-27.md) concluded that the single-tenant deployment path is complete but tenant development is not: a user added to a second tenant can log in there and still owns zero roles, because role bindings are stamped from the user's owning tenant and no assignment path exists across tenants; DeleteTenant permits deleting an active tenant once its active member count reaches zero, contradicting contract section 2.1; and AddMember accepts arbitrary user ids, so a phantom owner can displace the real last owner. This program converts the review into eight independently reviewable waves: two behavioural fixes (delete guard, member integrity), one decision plus its implementation for multi-membership authorization, one documentation/type alignment wave, one UI-automation wave, one plan-ladder decision and one dead-surface removal. No wave changes database schema, migrations, dependencies or pantheon-ops business code; every wave keeps the existing backend and frontend gate sets green.
findings: TC-01 (P1): a cross-tenant membership grants login but zero authorization. replaceUserRoles stamps system_user_role.tenant_id from the user's owning tenant (user_helper.go:83-108); RoleService.ensureUsersExist is tenant-scoped (role_helper.go:301-307); GetUserRolesForTenant filters bindings by the claimed tenant (login_runtime.go:328-338). A user added to tenant B via POST /system/tenant/B/members therefore resolves to an empty role set, an empty menu tree and 403 on every protected API, while the login picker and TenantSwitcher both offer that tenant.

TC-02 (P2): DeleteTenant requires 'has active members AND not archived' rather than 'not archived' (tenant_service.go:596-604). Deleting all users disables their memberships, after which an active tenant can be deleted without going through archived, contradicting contract sections 2.1 and 2.2.

TC-03 (P2): AddMember validates only that the tenant exists (tenant_service.go:858-903); tenant_memberships has no user foreign key (000013_tenant_canary.up.sql:48-59). An arbitrary or mistyped user id becomes a member, and a phantom owner row makes ensureNotLastOwner (tenant_service.go:948-975) allow removal of the real last owner.

TC-04 (P3): the platform tenant console has no automated UI coverage for tenant CRUD, archive/delete, member add/remove, the ops overview or the plan editor; smoke-tenant is push-only and report-only.
TC-05 (P3): TENANT_API.md documents an unmounted GET /system/tenant/:id/members/page compatibility alias (lines 229, 255) that exists only in the unmounted tenant_routes.go.
TC-06 (P3): MemberUsageQuery.status is typed 'active' | 'removed' (api.ts:239) while the UI sends 'disabled' (TenantMemberList.tsx:230-236) behind a cast that defeats type checking.
TC-07 (P3): the frontend plan capability ladder is hard-coded to four codes and unknown codes normalize to free (core/entitlements/plans.ts); registered in contract V1.5 as an explicit residual.

TC-08 (P3): tenant dead surface remains in the tree: tenant_handler.go + tenant_routes.go (unmounted in production, test-only), tenant_bootstrap.go (zero references), and MULTI_TENANT_DESIGN.md still describes subdomains, custom domains, branding and public registration as a next phase.

in: W1 2026-10-27-tenant-delete-archive-guard: delete only archived tenants; keep the in-transaction membership disable for archived tenants that still have active members; disable the UI delete action on non-archived rows; align contract, API doc and runbooks

W2 2026-10-27-tenant-member-integrity: reject unknown user ids in AddMember, count only real users in ensureNotLastOwner, replace the raw user-id input with a tenant-scoped user picker, and add regressions
W3 2026-10-27-tenant-multi-membership-decision: record the maintainer choice between narrowing membership semantics (A), adding cross-tenant role binding (B) and removing multi-tenant membership (C)

W4 2026-10-27-tenant-multi-membership-authorization: implement the decided option; the default packet implements A and additionally filters login candidates, auto-resolution and switchable tenants to those where the subject has at least one role

W5 2026-10-27-tenant-contract-docs-alignment: correct the unmounted members/page alias, fix the status union, mark MULTI_TENANT_DESIGN.md as vision-not-contract, and document owner transfer as add-owner then remove-owner
W6 2026-10-27-tenant-console-ui-automation: add Playwright coverage for the tenant console and strengthen the login-picker spec to assert usability, not just login success
W7 2026-10-27-tenant-plan-ladder-decision: decide keep-four-tier, server-driven entitlements, or remove plan UI gating; explicitly not part of V1 completeness
W8 2026-10-27-tenant-dead-surface-removal: delete the unmounted raw-JSON handler and routes and tenant_bootstrap.go, migrating their tests to the production handlers without losing coverage
Per-wave evidence under .harness/evidence/<wave-task-id>/ with commands.json, summary.md and review.md
Foundation release and base -> ops sync check after the program lands
out: Database schema, migrations, backfills or any data repair, including cleanup of historical cross-tenant membership rows
Billing, plan sale, upgrade/downgrade and billing periods (contract section 1 Out)
Independent schema/database, custom domains, branding and public registration
An implicit mapping from the membership role (owner/admin/member) to an IAM role, which contract section 2.2 forbids
Touching pantheon-ops business code; only compatibility verification is in scope
Reducing the exported surface of frontend/src/index.ts
Deleting or weakening tests to make a wave pass

implementationNotes: Wave order: W1 and W2 may run in parallel; W3 must precede W4; W5 runs after W1/W2/W4 so it documents the final behaviour; W6 depends on W1, W2 and the W3 decision; W7 and W8 may be scheduled independently.
W3 and W7 are decision packets, not implementation packets: the deliverable is a decision document, not a diff. W4 must not start before the maintainer signs W3.
Any new error code or i18n key introduced by W1 must be registered in contract section 5, TENANT_API.md and the frontend error mapping in the same wave; two out of three is an incomplete wave.
Filtering unusable tenant candidates and validating member writes are two ends of one defect: doing only one leaves the login picker offering a blank console.
Historical cross-tenant membership rows are out of scope. W4 may only stop new ones from being written and hide them from login candidates; a data-cleanup runbook is a separate packet.
One change class per commit so git bisect stays useful; W1's backend guard and frontend disable may share a wave but must be two commits.
The planner/dispatcher must not edit backend/ or frontend/src/; each wave must be executed by the Generator adapter and the handoff recorded in the manifest and evidence.
Refusals only where behaviour could change: a wave that cannot reproduce the review's failure case must close as abandoned with the reason, not as completed.

doNotTouch: the published tags and release assets

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Execute one wave per task packet through the Generator adapter; reproduce the review's failure case first, then fix it, then prove the gate set is green.
reviewerPosture: Confirm the wave reproduces the documented failure case before the fix and passes the same case after it.
Reject any wave that changes schema, migrations, permission codes, menus or i18n keys beyond the ones it declares.
Reject any wave that deletes or weakens a test instead of migrating it.
Confirm every new error code or i18n key is registered in contract, API doc and frontend mapping together.
Confirm pantheon-ops still builds after the foundation release sync.

commands: cd ../pantheon-ops && go build ./... && npm run build
runtimeEvidence: backend test summary before and after each behavioural wave (baseline: 46 ok, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP)
a failing-then-passing test name for TC-01, TC-02 and TC-03
login-candidate response snapshot before and after W4 for the same user and membership set

runtimeGap: No wave has started. This packet records the plan; all eight wave manifests are status=planned and no modified tree has been built or tested.
evidenceRequired: .harness/evidence/<wave-task-id>/commands.json with cwd, status and real output summary; anything not executed marked not-run with the reason
.harness/evidence/<wave-task-id>/summary.md with the change list, git diff --stat and the closed TC ids
.harness/evidence/<wave-task-id>/review.md with the pre-fix failure reproduction and the post-fix result
W6 Playwright output and screenshots, or not-run with the environment gap
humanGates: W1: confirm returning to the contract rule (delete only archived) instead of amending the contract wording.
W3: choose option A (narrow membership semantics), B (cross-tenant role binding) or C (single-tenant membership only).
W4: confirm the implementation scope against the W3 decision; if B or C is chosen, rewrite the packet before executing.
W6: decide whether smoke-tenant becomes a blocking gate, which is a CI policy change.
W7: decide whether the plan capability ladder becomes a V2 commercial workstream or stays as-is with quota thresholds only.
W8: approve the test-migration plan for the legacy handler so coverage does not drop.
completionChecklist: TC-02 closed: no non-archived tenant can be deleted; archived tenants remain deletable with active members
TC-03 closed: unknown user ids are rejected and phantom owner rows no longer count
TC-01 closed: login candidates, auto-resolution and switchable tenants never offer a tenant where the subject has no role; new memberships follow the W3 decision
TC-05 and TC-06 closed: API doc matches the mounted routes and the frontend status type matches the UI
TC-04 closed: the tenant console has automated UI coverage and the login-picker spec asserts usability
TC-07 decided (build or keep) and explicitly excluded from V1 completeness
TC-08 closed: dead entry points removed with coverage preserved and the design doc marked as vision
pantheon-ops builds against the synced foundation release
No schema, migration, permission code, menu or i18n key changed beyond the W1 error key
